title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Sentence-Level Chunking
summary: Sentence-level chunking uses NLP sentence boundary detection to split documents exactly at sentence boundaries, then groups sentences into chunks that fit within a size limit.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Sentence-level chunking uses NLP sentence boundary detection to split documents exactly at sentence boundaries, then groups sentences into chunks that fit within a size limit. This preserves sentence integrity — no chunk ever ends mid-sentence — making it semantically cleaner than fixed-size approaches. Libraries like NLTK, spaCy, and the `sentence-splitter` package handle edge cases like abbreviations (e.g., "Dr. Smith" should not split), decimal numbers (3.14), and multi-language sentence endings. The tradeoff is slightly higher processing cost (requires an NLP model pass) and potential chunk size variance (sentence lengths vary widely).

sections.title: ② Key Code
sections.body:
```python
import re
from typing import List
import spacy
from langchain_core.documents import Document

# Load spaCy English model
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

def sentence_chunk(text: str, max_tokens: int = 512, overlap_sentences: int = 1) -> List[str]:
    """
    Split text into chunks that respect sentence boundaries.
    Groups sentences until max_tokens is reached, with sentence-level overlap.
    """
    import tiktoken
    enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("text-embedding-3-large")
    
    # Detect sentence boundaries with spaCy
    doc = nlp(text)
    sentences = [sent.text.strip() for sent in doc.sents if sent.text.strip()]
    
    chunks = []
    current_chunk_sents = []
    current_tokens = 0
    
    for i, sentence in enumerate(sentences):
        sent_tokens = len(enc.encode(sentence))
        
        if current_tokens + sent_tokens > max_tokens and current_chunk_sents:
            # Save current chunk
            chunks.append(" ".join(current_chunk_sents))
            
            # Overlap: keep last N sentences
            current_chunk_sents = current_chunk_sents[-overlap_sentences:]
            current_tokens = sum(len(enc.encode(s)) for s in current_chunk_sents)
        
        current_chunk_sents.append(sentence)
        current_tokens += sent_tokens
    
    # Add final chunk
    if current_chunk_sents:
        chunks.append(" ".join(current_chunk_sents))
    
    return chunks

# Alternative: NLTK sentence tokenizer (lighter weight)
import nltk
nltk.download("punkt_tab", quiet=True)

def nltk_sentence_chunk(text: str, max_chars: int = 1000, overlap: int = 1) -> List[str]:
    """Sentence chunking using NLTK."""
    sentences = nltk.sent_tokenize(text)
    chunks = []
    current = []
    current_len = 0
    
    for sent in sentences:
        if current_len + len(sent) > max_chars and current:
            chunks.append(" ".join(current))
            current = current[-overlap:]
            current_len = sum(len(s) for s in current)
        
        current.append(sent)
        current_len += len(sent)
    
    if current:
        chunks.append(" ".join(current))
    
    return chunks

# Handle abbreviation edge cases
def robust_sentence_split(text: str) -> List[str]:
    """Handle tricky sentence boundaries."""
    # Protect abbreviations before splitting
    abbreviations = ["Dr.", "Mr.", "Mrs.", "Ms.", "Prof.", "Sr.", "Jr.", "vs.", "etc.", "Inc.", "Ltd.", "Fig."]
    
    protected_text = text
    placeholders = {}
    for i, abbr in enumerate(abbreviations):
        placeholder = f"ABBR{i}PLACEHOLDER"
        placeholders[placeholder] = abbr
        protected_text = protected_text.replace(abbr, placeholder)
    
    # Split on protected text
    sentences = nltk.sent_tokenize(protected_text)
    
    # Restore abbreviations
    restored = []
    for sent in sentences:
        for placeholder, abbr in placeholders.items():
            sent = sent.replace(placeholder, abbr)
        restored.append(sent)
    
    return restored
```

```
SENTENCE-LEVEL CHUNKING
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

INPUT TEXT:
"Dr. Smith reviewed the policy. Returns must be within 30 days.
Items must be in original packaging. Contact us at support@co.com.
Processing takes 5-7 business days. See Section 4.2 for exceptions."

STEP 1: SENTENCE DETECTION (spaCy/NLTK)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
S1: "Dr. Smith reviewed the policy."        (7 tokens)
S2: "Returns must be within 30 days."       (7 tokens)
S3: "Items must be in original packaging."  (7 tokens)
S4: "Contact us at support@co.com."         (6 tokens)
S5: "Processing takes 5-7 business days."   (7 tokens)
S6: "See Section 4.2 for exceptions."       (7 tokens)

NOTE: "Dr." did NOT split as a sentence boundary ✓
      "4.2" did NOT split as a sentence boundary ✓

STEP 2: GROUP INTO CHUNKS (max_tokens=20)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Chunk 1 (21 tokens — slight overflow, kept sentence intact):
  S1 + S2 + S3 = "Dr. Smith reviewed... 30 days. Items..."

Chunk 2 (1 sentence overlap):
  S3 (overlap) + S4 + S5 + S6:
  "Items must be in original... See Section 4.2..."

COMPARISON WITH FIXED CHUNKING:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Fixed char (100):  "Dr. Smith reviewed the policy. Returns must be within 30 da" ← CUT!
Sentence level:    "Dr. Smith reviewed the policy. Returns must be within 30 days." ← CLEAN ✓
```
